text:
sam_sales: Heads-up — LatticeBank POC hitting much higher TTFT than we promised. Median first token ~1.1s, target was 180ms. They're hitting bursts (short prompts, lots of small requests) on a Dedicated pool. We need a quick triage before EOD with customer call at 5pm PT.

emily_se: Ugh. Do we have example request_ids and a sample workload shape?

sam_sales: I pushed a couple request_ids to the thread. pattern: ~60 reqs/min, 1-2 token prompts mostly, model redwood-7b-8bit-q, concurrency set to 4. Request id: rq_20260301_42 and rq_20260301_43. Logs attached below.

ops-bot: log snippet for rq_20260301_42:
```
[2026-03-01T15:22:03Z] rq_id=rq_20260301_42 pool=lattice-dedicated model=redwood-7b-8bit-q seq_len=2 batch_size=1 batch_window_ms=20 kv_cache_hit=false cold_start_path=true latency_first_token_ms=1120
```

emily_se: That `kv_cache_hit=false` jump stands out — looks like every request is going down cold path. Are we intentionally disabling prefetch / prefix caching for this customer?

devon_infra: They were set up with prefetch=false to avoid memory pressure (asked by their infra team). Also batch_window_ms=20 (small) which causes a lot of tiny batches and hurts scheduler overhead. Two levers: enable prefetch/KV warmup or increase batch packing (bigger window or higher concurrency).

sanjay_runtime: Quick explainer: our runtime's steady-state TTFT relies on an active KV cache for short prompts. If prefetch is off and requests are random across many user ids we can't reuse KV entries and every request triggers the full decode cold path. For short prompts the scheduler overhead + cold path cost dominates.

sam_sales: Customer is sensitive about memory; they explicitly asked to avoid preloading. Can we propose a middle ground?

devon_infra: Yes — suggest enabling `prefetch=on` but with `max_prefetch_per_gpu=2` and `prefetch_ttl=60s`. That keeps memory low but helps reuse for bursty traffic. Also reduce `batch_window_ms` to 8 and bump concurrency to 6. Command to apply (internal):
```
redwoodctl update-pool --name lattice-dedicated --set prefetch=true --set max_prefetch_per_gpu=2 --set prefetch_ttl=60 --set batch_window_ms=8 --set concurrency=6
```

maria_support: I'll ask LatticeBank if they're OK with a conservative prefetch. I can also gather which user ids hit most often so we can scope prefetching to top prefixes (less memory).

aj_pricing: If they need higher concurrency for the POC window we can offer a short-term burst add-on at a discounted rate instead of changing their Dedicated commit. Happy to draft pricing.

ingrid_pm: Also FYI the security team asked whether enabling prefetch affects KMS or data residency — customer wants keys in their KMS. Does prefetching cache decrypted token context in GPU memory?

sanjay_runtime: Prefetch caches model KV state (keys/values) derived from tokens, not plaintext customer data. KMS only protects stored secrets; runtime never offloads plaintext prompts to disk when using our private KMS integration. Enabling prefetch doesn't change KMS posture.

emily_se: Practical next steps for the call: 1) prod apply conservative prefetch + smaller batch window as devon suggested, 2) run 10m synthetic burst test, 3) monitor `latency_first_token_ms` and `kv_cache_hit` metrics in console live. Can ops run the apply in staging and then prod if green?

devon_infra: Staging done in ~10m. I'll run the config change in staging now and post results.

ops-bot: staging change applied to pool lattice-dedicated-staging (prefetch=true, max_prefetch_per_gpu=2, batch_window_ms=8, concurrency=6).

ops-bot: staging test results (1m sample):
```
median_latency_first_token_ms=140
kv_cache_hit_rate=86%
```

sam_sales: Nice — 140ms median on staging looks good. Can we expect slightly worse in prod due to noise? I'll tell LatticeBank ~180-250ms expected.

maria_support: I'll update them and request permission to apply to prod for a 2-hour smoke window.

aj_pricing: Also proposing we include a 2-week 15% credit on extra burst nodes used during the POC to offset their risk. If they accept we can enable immediate burst capacity.

ingrid_pm: Customer also emailed a short security questionnaire about key rotation cadence and audit logs. I can handle that while we do the perf work.

sanjay_runtime: One more runtime note: if customer traffic is highly sharded by user-id we should consider sticky routing to keep requests pinned to GPUs that have the KV entries, that reduces cross-shard misses. It's a small infra change but high ROI for short prompts.

devon_infra: Sticky routing needs a quick config flip on the routing policy; low risk. I'll prepare the change but only enable after prod smoke confirmation.

sam_sales: Thanks all. Plan: apply conservative prefetch in prod on approval, run 10m smoke, enable sticky routing if still noisy, offer burst credit if they ask, Ingrid handles security Qs, Maria coordinates customer. 5pm PT call — I'll start with the staging numbers and recommend the change. :thumbsup:

emily_se: Thanks team — please ping here when prod smoke is green so I can share live graphs on the call.

ops-bot: prod change queued; awaiting approval from oncall to proceed.
